scenes.headline: What is Python?
scenes.subtitle: The readable language that ties modern data engineering together
scenes.narration: Python is a high-level, readable programming language that has become the everyday tool for building data pipelines.

scenes.headline: Why data engineers live in Python
items: Glue for databases, APIs and files
Runs on laptops, containers and clusters
scenes.narration: Its clean syntax means you spend more time thinking about data and less time fighting the language. A rich ecosystem of libraries like pandas, PySpark and Airflow covers almost every data task you will meet. Because it connects databases, APIs and files so easily, Python acts as the glue between the systems in a pipeline. And the same code runs on your laptop, inside a container, or across a distributed cluster.

scenes.headline: Readable by design
scenes.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("orders.csv")
big = df[df["amount"] > 100]

print(big.groupby("region")["amount"].sum())
scenes.narration: Here we import pandas, then load an orders file into a table with a single call. The next line keeps only the rows where the amount is above one hundred. Finally we group those large orders by region and sum their amounts, so a real analysis fits in just a few readable lines.

scenes.headline: Python is the glue of the pipeline
scenes.narration: A pipeline starts by pulling data from sources such as APIs and databases. Python then extracts and transforms that raw data into a clean, consistent shape. From there it loads the results into a warehouse or lake, where analytics and machine learning teams put the data to work.

scenes.headline: Interpreted and dynamic, with trade-offs

columns.title: Watch-outs
points: Slower than compiled C or Java

scenes.narration: Being interpreted and dynamic makes Python quick to write and easy to change, which is why prototypes come together so fast. The trade-off is raw speed, since it runs slower than compiled languages and the global interpreter lock limits CPU-bound threads. For most work that is fine, but at large scale you push the heavy lifting down to vectorized libraries and engines like Spark.

scenes.text: If you learn one language for data engineering, make it Python.
scenes.narration: The bottom line is simple: if you learn just one language for data engineering, make it Python.
